textbookText: A. Choose the best alternative. Which of the following is not correctly classified as a type of biomolecule? a) Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and nucleic acids b) Water, minerals, ions, and salts c) Water, carbon dioxide, and salts d) Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats What is the general formula for carbohydrates? a) Cx(H2O)y b) CHxO c) CnH2nO2 d) CnH2On Which of the following is a disaccharide? a) Glucose b) Sucrose c) Ribose d) Fructose Polysaccharides are characterized by: a) Sweet taste and water solubility b) Composed of 2-10 monosaccharides c) Long chains of monosaccharides with no reducing properties d) Being aldoses or ketoses What is the significance of monosaccharides like ribose and deoxyribose in cellular function? a) They serve as structural elements in RNA and DNA. b) They provide energy through breakdown. c) They support the synthesis of proteins and nucleic acids. d) They prevent the formation of ketone bodies in the blood.
Why is glycogen considered essential in animal metabolism? a) It forms the plant cell wall, providing structural support.
b) It supports the synthesis of fats and amino acids. c) It prevents the incomplete oxidation of fats. d) It serves as a primary reserve food stored in the liver and muscles.

Which of the following groups of amino acids must be obtained from the diet because the human body cannot produce them? a) Alanine, arginine, asparagine b) Histidine, isoleucine, leucine c) Glutamic acid, glutamine, glycine d) Aspartic acid, cysteine, tyrosine What is the primary function of tyrosine among amino acids? a) As a precursor to synthesize animal hormones like thyroxine and adrenaline b) Acting as the building block for protein synthesis c) Acting as a precursor for the plant hormone Indole Acetic Acid (IAA) d) Being essential for the synthesis of melanin pigments Which category of proteins is formed by the combination of amino acids and nucleic acids? a) Simple proteins b) Conjugated proteins c) Derived proteins d) Fibrous proteins Which type of protein exhibits a twisted structure and forms fiber-like arrangements? a) Primary structure b) Secondary structure c) Tertiary structure d) Quaternary structure What is the primary characteristic of fibrous proteins? a) They are predominantly found in plants. b) They exhibit a twisted structure and form fiber-like arrangements. c) They are soluble in water, salt solutions, acids, or bases. d) They are formed by the combination of amino acids and nucleic acids.

Which function of proteins involves regulating glucose levels in the body? a) Acting as structural proteins for building and repairing tissues b) Providing energy fuel with a caloric value of 5.65 kcal per gram c) Acting as enzymes or biocatalysts to regulate life processes d) Functioning as hormones like insulin Which category of lipids is primarily found in animal products like meat and dairy, as well as in some plant-based oils like coconut oil and palm oil? a) Simple lipids b) Complex or conjugated lipids c) Derived lipids d) Waxes Which type of fatty acids generally have lower melting points and are often in liquid state (oil) at room temperature? a) Unsaturated fatty acids b) Saturated fatty acids c) Monounsaturated fatty acids d) Polyunsaturated fatty acids Which complex lipid is a key component of cell membranes and white matter in nerve tissue? a) Glycolipids b) Phospholipids c) Lipoprotein d) Cholesterol Which derived lipid acts as a precursor for sex hormones like progesterone, testosterone, and cortisol? a) Cholesterol b) Fatty acids c) Sterols d) Glycerides Biology, Grade 11 | 31
Which type of RNA carries coded information to synthesize polypeptide chains? a) Messenger RNA (mRNA) b) Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) c) Transfer RNA (tRNA) d) Viral RNA
14. Which type of sugar is found in RNA nucleotides? a. Deoxyribose b. Ribose c. Glucose d. Fructose

Which component is present in both DNA and RNA nucleotides? a) Deoxyribose sugar b) Ribose sugar c) Phosphoric acid d) Thymine Which of the following minerals contributes to the formation of chlorophyll pigment? a) Sodium (Na) b) Iron (Fe) c) Magnesium (Mg) d) Iodine (I)
Which trace element is essential for the hormone thyroxine and deficiency can lead to goiter? a) Copper (Cu) b) Iron (Fe) c) Iodine (I) d) Manganese (Mn)

Which characteristic of enzymes allows them to catalyze only a certain reaction? a) They are usually globular proteins b) They are highly specific c) They can include inorganic or organic substances for their activity Biology, Grade 11 | 32
